subStrands.name: Rationale, Development, Careers and Cultural Values

objectives.description: Meaning and rationale for studying textiles; developments of textiles and careers; textiles and cultural values; competencies, attitudes and behaviour required for employment.
Identification and classification of fibres; properties and suitability; fibre processing (soaking, ginning, etc.).
Yarn preparation (traditional and contemporary); types of yarn; blends and mixtures; yarn terminologies.
Point paper designing: plain, twill, satin/sateen and variations.
Looms and accessories: types of loom (man power, traditional, broad loom and power looms — shuttle and shuttle-less — and accessories); textile calculations (weight/cost of warp, weft and fabric).
Weaving processes (traditional and broad loom): warping, beaming, heddling, reeding, tying up, bobbin winding; loom motions (primary, secondary and auxiliary).
Other fabric construction processes: knitting, crocheting and tapestry; non-woven fabric.

Preparation, care and maintenance of tools, materials and equipment; basic drawings using elements and principles of design; idea development/preliminary designing/ICT; usage of indigenous colour schemes, ideas, symbols and cultural motifs.
Decorative techniques: dyeing, printing, appliqué and embroidery processes; types of finishing techniques (mechanical and chemical); care and maintenance of fabrics.
Sustainable development: challenges and interventions in managing resources, marketing and distribution; cultural values (traditional/contemporary); healthy studio practices.

Portfolio and Exhibition: types of portfolios (hard and soft copy); collection and building of portfolio; meaning, types, purpose and processes of mounting exhibitions; appreciating and patronising indigenous textiles.
Entrepreneurial skills in practice: preparation of business plan; planning of an enterprise; key points of a business plan; costing, pricing and marketing of textile products.
